transcript: The other night, I saw Orlando at Signature Theatre. Described as “a theatrical, wild, fantastical, trip through space, time, and gender” this play by Sarah Ruhl follows the journey of the titular character Orlando, here played by Taylor Mac. Orlando lives for centuries inhabiting many places and undergoing a lot of personal changes including becoming a woman partway through the play. A small ensemble of actors play over a dozen other characters that Orlando encounters and they all collectively narrate the story like a Greek chorus. This style of direct and collective narration isn't my favorite, and unfortunately I was really tired when I saw this. So it took me a bit to get into the groove of things and start following but I anchored myself in admiring the ensemble work here which is super fun and the joy that this cast exudes is just infectious. Other highlights of the production for me included the striking costuming and the unexpected choreographed moments which are very fun and campy. With that, another program for my collection.
